U.S. Army AFT

Army Fitness Test

Illustrative training photograph

FITNESS TEST

At a glance

The Army Fitness Test combines five strength, endurance and running events. It is distinct from the Ranger selection programme and from the separate Combat Field Test.

FEATURED ACTIVITYTwo-mile runUse the published scoring table for your category

What the test includes

  • Three-repetition maximum deadlift
  • Hand-release push-up
  • Sprint-drag-carry
  • Plank
  • Two-mile run

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

The five-event Army Fitness Test replaced the ACFT in June 2025. Use the current AFT score scale, not the former six-event test.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

EventResult recordedPractice focus
3-repetition maximum deadliftLoad60 lb hex bar plus plates; three controlled repetitions
Hand-release push-upValid repetitions in 2 minutesFull arm extension while prone between repetitions
Sprint-drag-carryElapsed time over 250 mFive 50 m out-and-back shuttles: sprint, drag, lateral, carry, sprint; 90 lb sled and two 40 lb kettlebells
PlankHold durationStable trunk position
Two-mile runElapsed timeMeasured, generally flat outdoor route of approximately 3.22 km

Scoring and scope

Army guidance sets a 60-point minimum per event and 300 total for combat-enabling specialties; designated combat specialties require 350 total with at least 60 per event. Use the current applicable age/category tables and check any later policy or exemptions. The Combat Field Test is separate.

  • Official AFT scoring tables and instructions

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Build foundational strength before heavy triples. Use coaching and suitable equipment; avoid frequent maximal attempts.
  • Practise hand-release push-up form and controlled plank intervals. Learn sprint-drag-carry movements separately before timing a full sequence.
  • Combine easy runs and one paced interval session as tolerated. Rehearse event order below maximum effort before a formal assessment.

Putting it into a training week

Practise a short block of each movement and log it before combining events. Use low-volume technique sessions for loaded events and save hard efforts for a planned rehearsal.

Common mistakes

  • Using legacy ACFT scoring or adding the discontinued power throw.
  • Practising only the two-mile run, or letting fatigue compromise deadlift technique.

What to log

Record category, lifted load, valid repetitions, sprint-drag-carry time, plank duration and run time.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.

Worth knowing

  • The applicable scoring and testing requirements depend on the current Army rules and the person’s category.
  • Check the scoring tables and instructions before attempting a practice test.
